utterances.text: Since the analysis of combat readiness implies that background material has been received in time and evaluations had been provided previously by subordinate commanders, practically all the organs cooperate and write together and gather all the oral information collected previously. Based on that, they write their conclusions and proposals of tasks and present it -- present it here in a shortened form -- [microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did the organs in charge of operational matters who did this work were also in charge of formulating the contents of the proposals?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the speakers who presented the content of proposals. They were in charge of formulating and sorting these proposals, and the speakers were commanders, assistant commanders. There is a whole group determined there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown page 5 in English, and for B/C/S it's still page 3. We can see at the bottom of the page the name of Colonel Miletic, just at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did Colonel Miletic determine the content of specific interventions indicated in this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, I don't know if we're talking about something on a theoretical level or we're talking about something that's peculiar to the facts of this case, and I would suggest that if that's the nature of the question that it's inappropriate to put to the expert unless there is some foundation for it. Otherwise, if it's just talking about the signature on the document as a matter of form rather than a matter of factual substance, then I think the question would otherwise be appropriate. But I just wanted to clarify that and make sure that it ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Fauveau, do you wish to comment?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I am speaking about the rules concerning the usual methods of work. I don't know about this specific situation how General Miletic did it and had to do and how he could do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question was directed to the specific -- the content of the specific interventions indicated in the document, and unless this witness has some direct knowledge of the circumstances concerning the contents of this document, the question would be inappropriate and would call for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She is going to reformulate --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will reformulate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, because I think basically after having heard him the second time, I think he is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: How is this sort of document normally elaborated?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Analysis of combat readiness is a normal action, normal procedure defined by structure, and in terms of structure it would not be different than any other army. It has its own elements of combat readiness; there is a stipulated way of making proposals, of drawing conclusions, and settling the matter. Every point in the analysis of combat readiness is prescribed in advance, a skeleton already exists, and everybody just makes specific proposals in their area. Let's take as an example problems of financing -- planning, development, and financing of the VRS in 1994. It would be the chief for planning and development who would fill in this box, make this proposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown 5D1206. This is an order from the Main Staff, 23 January 1995. Just before I ask my question, could the witness be shown the last page of the document. We can see here that this document bears the name of the commander, General Mladic. I would like now to come back to page 11 of this document. Page 1, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The plan of the analysis for the combat readiness which we saw a while ago and which bore the name of General Miletic, was it or should it have been linked in any way to this order of General Mladic? Should it have been connected?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We must decipher the methodology of maintaining the analysis of combat readiness. There are several more elements here. The analysis of combat readiness for a certain year is usually part of the annual plan as well. As we can see, the order of the commander of the VRS invokes that plan. This analysis is made according to a certain skeleton and methodolgy. The commander defines the obligations of all the executive components. When the commanders of subordinate units submit their own results, a draft plan of implementation is created.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We haven't heard the President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Sorry, I had the microphone switched off. Go ahead, I think we have got everything now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Once this draft plan of the analysis of combat readiness is made - that's the plan we reviewed previously - the draft is submitted to the commander who agrees on it, gets the approval with the supreme commander because no plan must be contrary to the decisions of the supreme commander. Then, it is returned for final technical processing, and it awaits all the participants on the table when they come for a final analysis.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown page 3 in B/C/S of this decision. In English, it would be page 5. We have seen that the chief of the organ in charge of education and administration had a role in the preparation of this meeting for analysis of the combat readiness of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did other organs of the command -- did they take part in the preparation of this analysis?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we know what the analysis of combat readiness consists of, if we know that it comprises all the elements, all the same elements that the command consists of, then we know that not only were they involved other organs of the command, they actually proposed their own elements; thus, Mr. Djukic of the logistics was the proponent for the security of General Tolimir, and the chief of operations and training was the proponent of passages dealing with operations and training.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at number 8, which is on the last page, page 6 of the English text. According to this number 8, after -- at the end of the meeting, the commanders of units were to transmit to the chief of administration in charge of operational questions and instruction, education, the analysis prepared for combat preparedness made in 1994. Which unit is mentioned here? Which units are we speaking here?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are unit commanders directly subordinated to the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska. It relates to the ground forces, the ground corps, the airforce, regiments, and brigade, the school centre, Rajko Balic, and other units. I'm not sure because I don't see the mobilization trail. But those are the units that are directly subordinated.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown now 5D1207. This is an order from the Main Staff dated 25 January 1995 which bears the name of General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please look at number 2 of this order --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- page 2 for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In this paragraph, the tasks of the assistant of the commander for logistics was determined -- the tasks were determined. How does the assistant of the commander for security, since this order has the name of General Tolimir, could determine the tasks of the assistant commander for logistics? How is it possible?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know that the analysis of combat readiness is an activity where all commanders on the operative and tactical levels attend. Even heads of state often attend. That fact in itself indicates that it is a very risky moment, something that could be lethal to the unit. In these analyses, measures of security are much more stringent than in a regular situation. This is the task of the chief of security. He insisted here on stricter methods of security and proposed guard duty, which is not strictly within his competence, but everybody understood that it was necessary, and nobody minded that he overstepped his authority a little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We have a reference in the transcript, I think it's at line 22, where the expert mentions the chief of security. In the context of this order that's signed by General Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- I just want to clarify that we are talking about assistant commander for intelligence and security as distinguished from chief of security within the structure of the Main Staff, just so that the record is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Also for the record, because he keeps saying -- I mean, there is something which makes it obvious to me that the page and lines that I have are not tallying with yours, for sure, but in any case that will be checked later. What I have here is page 24, line 4. Otherwise, do you agree with -- not do you agree. Actually, I think it's a valid point. If you could pursue it with the witness, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I entirely agree on the function of General Tolimir. I entirely agree with my colleague from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's proceed then.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Why did the meetings concerning readiness for combat, why were they organised?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said more than once, they were held in order to make a good decision, and in order to successfully command, one must be well-acquainted with the status and condition of your units, and you will best be able to assess the situation of your units if you get the reports on combat readiness. This is like an X-ray, and the analysis of the combat readiness was that X-ray for the commander of the VRS, and with it he knew what to do next. You will see that this is correct when you see the document when he defined further tasks, after this analysis, and decided that combat readiness should be raised to a higher level.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you tell us during which period these meetings were normally organised, these meetings concerning readiness for combat? What was their frequency?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the strategic and operative level, the analysis of combat readiness is done once a year, normally at the end of the year for the year past; and for lower levels, it's done more frequently.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D966. This is an order from the Drina Corps dated 17 January 1995 concerning the analysis of the combat readiness of the Drina Corps. Could you look at number 5 in this order on page 2. In this paragraph number 5, you can read first of all: "[In English] All organs and sectors of the corps command will prepare for the annual analysis according to their functions and present for the purposes a joint analysis the necessary summaries and charts in order to obtain a better picture of the situation in the corps in 1994. "The corps command operations and training will be in charge of preparing the analysis, and all questions should be addressed to them."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you explain, what was the role of the organ in charge of operational and education for the preparation of analysis, according to this order?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The role of the operations and training organ in command of the Drina Corps, and here in paragraph 5, is defined exactly as I explained the role of that organ and the level of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. I don't want to -- in fact, I will tell you about the specific task that the commander issued, that everybody, according to their function, prepare a report and schematic that is necessary to evaluate the situation; and then, together with the Assistant Chief of Staff for Operations and Training, he would define it and put it together into a whole where he would determine the sequence, the terminology, the time and place, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to page 1 of this order. At number 2, you can see the elements of combat readiness. I think there is a translation mistake concerning the third element, which is the education, which has not been accurately translated into English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So could you read out to us in B/C/S the components for combat readiness.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I've not received the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first element is control and command. The first element of combat readiness is control and command; the second element is moral guidance, religious, and legal affairs; the third element of combat readiness is combat training and education; the fourth element is mobilisation, or mobilisational, organisational, financial, and personnel support and affairs; the next one is logistical support; after that, intelligence and security support; and the last element is administrative and office management. We can conclude that this fourth element is mobilisational, organisational, establishment, and staffing or personnel affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1394. This is an analysis of combat readiness for the Drina Corps in 1994. 5D1394.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This document bears the date of 28th January, 1995. According to what we've seen in the Main Staff documents and according to your experience, do the elements of this analysis, do they have to be presented during the analysis of the combat readiness of the Army of the Republika Srpska which was supposed to take place on the 29th and the 30th of January?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is always precisely established by a methodolgy that subordinate corps should submit their written analysis before the analysis taken at the level of the Main Staff. Each organ reviews this analysis within their respective purview, and the commander should also present their own analysis. In this context, this should have preceded the analysis carried out at the Main Staff of the VRS, and all the officers in charge should be able to review this analysis.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could page 20 in B/C/S be shown, please, and page 22 for the English text.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So one sees at the bottom of the page what are the main assignments in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if we could show the very bottom, please, just a little further down.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: According to assignment number 4, the corps command is to find a way to completely close off the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves. Who ascertained that assignment for the Drina Corps in January 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This task was signed to the Drina Corps in 1993, and it was a continuous task, but it practically was never completed until the separation of the enclave in July.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you know, just to elaborate a little bit on what you just said --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown Exhibit 5D988. This is the monthly plan for the Drina Corps for November 1994. Under item 3, one sees that the complete close-off of the Srebrenica enclave was one of the main assignment for the Drina Corps in November 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is this in line with what you said before?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. It appears in various forms. I am only surprised how this could have been one of the main tasks for months and years without it being completely finalised. They are speaking here of closing off the Srebrenica enclave, which automatically involves the separation of the enclave. This task is formulated in different ways, but the basics and the fundamental and essential meaning was there, but it was never completed and achieved.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now come back to Exhibit 5D1394, i.e., the analysis for combat readiness of the Drina Corps. I would like to have page 21 in B/C/S, 23 in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In the very last part of this document, the Drina Corps suggests that the supreme commander be given to -- in the Main Staff find a solution for the elimination of enclaves. Now, is such a proposal normal -- such a proposition of a subordinate unit a regular or a normal one?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This proposal is an unusual one and out of the context. If someone gives you an order to make a separation this year and then two years later you come up with a proposal for elimination, this is out of a military context.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And do you see a link between this proposition and Directive number 7?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any connection between the Directive 7/1 because this one that refers to the enclaves is very precise and clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I don't know if it was a translation error, but the question was put specifically with respect to Directive number 7 and the answer responds Directive 7/1. I wonder if we could clarify that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose that the witness must have heard the question that it was related to Directive number 7. What I want to know is whether in his reply, in his answer, he referred to Directive number 7 or to Directive number 7/1. And you are the one who can tell us that, General.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both Directive number 7 and number 7/1 were precise and accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye. It doesn't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's not responsive to the question that was put by my colleague, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I am going to leave it in your hands, Ms. Fauveau, because I wouldn't like to interfere here.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we limit ourselves to Directive 7. So I would like to ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What about the proposition of the Drina Corps? Could it have an influence or a link with Directive number 7?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This proposal from the Drina Corps - actually, it's item number 1 - has no bearing on Directive number 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show you now Exhibit 5D1208. This is an order from the Main Staff from 16th of February, 1995, and I -- with the name of General Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you please have a look at this order and tell us whether this order is one way or another connected to the analysis about combat readiness which was performed at the end of January?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the content, this has nothing to do with the analysis of combat readiness conducted in that period. This is a daily order of a completely different type where information about the enemy is required.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could this order have had a link with the preparation of Directive number 7?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the contents, it is possible because they are looking to see what the balance of forces is, which would serve as a basis for proposing further activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Can we leave it at that for today because I need to show an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I intervened, in fact. General, we are going to stop here. We will resume again tomorrow morning, same advisory as yesterday. Please do not contact or discuss this with anyone until you finish your testimony. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00.
